title_original: Steven Spielberg to Direct The Heart in Winter from Paul Thomas Anderson Script; Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley, and Mark Rylance Among Ensemble

blocks.text: Word of Steven Spielberg’s western has been perpetuated by none other than the man himself, and just after Janusz Kamiński offered a small update , the project is moving forward in expectedly major ways. Per Deadline , his first oater will by scripted by Paul Thomas Anderson, star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley, and Mark Rylance, and adapt Kevin Barry’s novel The Heart in Winter , a project that emerged from ongoing talk of collaboration and watching a bevy of westerns on 35mm. As Spielberg elaborated:

“It’s really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team.”

Between this and What Happens at Night (to say nothing of uncredited work on Killers of the Flower Moon ) it’s nice seeing Anderson become a New Hollywood whisperer. (Not that they need it, but still.) Production is expected to begin in winter of 2027 under the aegis of Universal, with a 2028 release from Focus Features.
For a sense of where Spielberg and Anderson are headed, read a synopsis of The Heart in Winter below (via Penguin ):

October 1891. A hard winter approaches across the Rocky Mountains. The city of Butte, Montana is rich on copper mines and rampant with vice and debauchery among a hard-living crowd of immigrant Irish workers. Here we find Tom Rourke, a young poet and ballad-maker of the town, but also a doper, a drinker, and a fearsome degenerate. Just as he feels his life is heading nowhere fast, Polly Gillespie arrives in town as the new bride of the extremely devout mine captain Long Anthony Harrington. A thunderbolt love affair takes spark between Tom and Polly and they strike out west on a stolen horse, moving through the badlands of Montana and Idaho, and briefly an idyll of wild romance perfects itself. But a posse of deranged Cornish gunmen are soon in hot pursuit and closing in fast. With everything to lose and the safety and anonymity of San Francisco still a distant speck on their horizon, the choices they make will haunt them for the rest of their lives.
